zod-5775.text:
GOAL
Keep public constructor types honest across Classic and Mini without changing valid runtime behavior. Invalid schema compositions should fail at the public call site, while valid shapes retain precise inference and bundle parity.

PROVEN APPROACH
Two immediately prior, authentic fixes repaired type-only drift by tightening the narrow public generic rather than adding runtime guards. Commit 757f0b0f made strictObject and looseObject apply the same Writeable shape normalization as object, then proved the displayed shape without changing runtime output. Commit fa4a3740 extended that contract across Classic and Mini object constructors and transformations, with compile-time assertions on both bundles. The reusable pattern is: identify the public generic that currently admits the invalid shape, constrain it using the discriminator already supplied to the API, and mirror the constraint on the Mini surface. Preserve inference for valid literals and keep runtime selection untouched unless a runtime probe independently demonstrates a defect.

PROVING EVIDENCE
Before editing, compile one invalid option that lacks the requested discriminator and one valid multi-option union. The invalid option must currently be accepted, establishing the static regression, while the valid control must compile and parse. After the final edit, the invalid call must produce a TypeScript error that is consumed by an explicit expect-error, and the valid Classic control must still compile and run. Then close the independently qualified Mini compile-time parity check. Existing discriminated-union runtime tests remain the regression surface, but a green runtime suite alone cannot prove this issue because the reported failure is late detection rather than incorrect parsing of a valid union.

APPLICABILITY BOUNDARY
Use this episode only when a public generic accepts a structurally invalid option that the API's own discriminator parameter can name. Do not ban empty or otherwise valid constructions not covered by the issue, do not weaken options to any, and do not add a runtime-only throw as a substitute for the compile-time contract. Treat Classic and Mini as separate public consumers: a Classic-only type fix is incomplete when both expose the same constructor. Prefer the smallest signature-level change that preserves valid literal inference.

obligations.description: Inspect the prior Classic/Mini public generic parity repair before choosing an ownership surface.
Typecheck the Classic discriminated-union option boundary after the latest edit.
Preserve the same compile-time discriminator boundary through the Mini public surface.

contrastive_probe.claim: Classic discriminatedUnion must reject an option missing its named discriminator at compile time while retaining precise inference for a valid option.
contrastive_probe.falsifier: Reject a runtime-only guard, an any-shaped signature, or a constraint that also makes a valid literal-discriminated option fail to compile.

artifact.content: import{spawnSync}from"node:child_process";import{writeFileSync,rmSync}from"node:fs";const path="packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/hunch-zod-5775-classic-static.test.ts";const source=`import {test} from "vitest";import * as z from "zod/v4";const valid=z.discriminatedUnion("kind",[z.object({kind:z.literal("ok"),value:z.string()})]);type Input=z.input<typeof valid>;const control:Input={kind:"ok",value:"yes"};// @ts-expect-error missing named discriminator\nz.discriminatedUnion("kind",[z.object({value:z.string()})]);test("valid control",()=>{valid.parse(control)});`;writeFileSync(path,source);const result=spawnSync("npx",["vitest","--typecheck","run",path],{encoding:"utf8",env:{...process.env,CI:"true"}});rmSync(path,{force:true});console.log(`HUNCH_CONTRAST classic-static-discriminator state=${result.status===0?"green":"red"}`);

contract_axis_probes.claim: Mini discriminatedUnion must enforce the same named-discriminator option constraint as Classic without rejecting a valid Mini literal option.
contract_axis_probes.falsifier: Reject a Classic-only fix, a generic Mini base-type edit, or a Mini signature that loses precise inference for valid options.
